results.name: 134 new variants in 17 families; legacy IDs remain unique and available
Every new variant validates, retains geometry and metadata through JSON, and exports
Every new part preserves pin numbers and coordinates after four rotations and two flips
Placed footprints are snapshots, not live library references
NE555 and LM358 PDIP and SOIC pin maps agree with numbered reference vectors
74HC595 signal and supply pin numbers are retained
MCP23017 uses narrow SPDIP-28 with pins 11/14 NC and 12/13 I2C
ULN2803C is DW-20, not an incorrectly substituted 18-pin device
Named onsemi transistors have E-B-C pin roles and no guessed net
Regulator pin map and physical tab identity are explicit
Qwiic labels do not assign or merge electrical nets
PH, XH and SH remain distinct physical pitches
USB4085 has 16 unique signal contacts plus four explicitly common shell terminals
Narrow USB shell slots keep their reference width and obey a stricter manufacturer profile
Editing names leaves geometry, number, polarity and assigned net unchanged
Internal-terminal net conflicts are reported as errors, not invisibly merged
Internal groups do not create invisible PCB copper or satisfy unrouted nets
Source metadata rejects executable links and malformed terminal references
NC assignments produce a warning; a functional pin name is not a circuit rule
User review can acknowledge nominal geometry, but new label edits clear that status
Uno ICSP appends six pads without touching any of the original 32
Uno ICSP top-view coordinates are invariant between shield and carrier templates
Unused ICSP removal restores the exact old pin set; net or copper use prevents removal
ICSP option rejects unrelated host families
Encoder mechanical fixing holes follow transforms and remain NPTH
New polarity is printed independently of editor pin-name visibility
Pin-map CSV escapes formula-leading user labels
The catalog can be searched by family, manufacturer and functional pin
